newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER BLASTS BAYERN AFTER 5-2 THRASHING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER BLASTS BAYERN AFTER 5-2 THRASHING.

text.p: Bayern Munich chairman Franz Beckenbauer launched a fierce attack on his team after they suffered a calamitous 5-2 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday to lose vital ground in the German league title race.

"We are going to have to find another word for what we produced today because it wasn't football," the former World Cup-winning coach and captain said. "There was no commitment there. We practically invited Leverkusen to score goals."

The crushing defeat of Bayern enabled reigning champions and European Cup quarter-finalists Borussia Dortmund to finish the weekend top of the table, having won 2-1 at bottom club Freiburg on Saturday.
Bayern, who started the weekend with a three-point lead at the top, are level on points but have slipped to second place because of an inferior goal difference.

Leverkusen, who were involved in an intense battle to avoid relegation last season, exposed huge holes in the Bavarians' defence, hitting three goals in the first half alone through Brazilian Paulo Sergio, Rene Rydlewicz and Markus Feldhoff.
Bayern made a brief comeback in the second half with goals from Christian Nerlinger and international midfielder Mario Basler to narrow the home side's lead to 3-2.
But Feldhoff struck again from close range in the 80th minute at a corner and then raced away on his own four minutes later to complete his hat-trick.
"The first half was decisive for the result," Bayern captain Lothar Matthaeus said. "Leverkusen's attitude was better. We were told to go out aggressively but we didn't do what we should have done."
Asked to comment on Beckenbauer's attack, Germany's former World Cup captain said: "It's difficult to say anything after you've just lost 5-2. The boss is always right."
Leverkusen, third in the table just two points behind the leading duo, stayed out on the pitch after the final whistle to enjoy a huge celebration with their fans.
Sergio turned superbly in the area to fire the ball into the right-hand corner for their opening goal in the fifth minute.

The Bayern defence looked very disorganised for the second in the 37th minute when libero Jens Nowotny struck an accurate cross from the left and Rydlewicz hit his left-foot shot crisply inside the right-hand post.
Leverkusen needed a bit of luck with their third goal six minute later. Carsten Ramelow failed to time his long-range shot properly but Feldhoff stuck out his foot to deflect the ball into the net.

For a moment in the second half Bayern seemed to be coming back into the match. Nerlinger fired home a crisp volley in the 64th minute and Basler's long-range free-kick was deflected into the net in the 71st.
But it was never going to be Bayern's night. The little-known Feldhoff, a Bayern fan in his youth, took advantage of their lack of discipline at the back to seal victory with his two late goals.
